title: Entanglement dynamics through electromagnetic interactions in single-electron traps
authors: Pablo Guillermo Carmona Rufo, Anupam Mazumdar, Carlos Sabín
abstract: We study the dynamics of quantum entanglement between two harmonically trapped electrons interacting via the electromagnetic force. Starting from two-mode Gaussian states at thermal equilibrium, we make use of the covariance matrix formalism in order to compute the logarithmic negativity of the evolved state as a quantitative measure of entanglement. We analyze two initial configurations: thermal single-mode and two-mode squeezed states, and describe the time evolution of entanglement in the system for different values of squeezing and temperature, while identifying the parameter regimes accessible to current and near-future single-electron trap experiments.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes the dynamics of quantum entanglement between two interacting electrons confined in harmonic traps. Using Gaussian state formalism, it calculates entanglement evolution via logarithmic negativity for different initial squeezing conditions. The results show that electromagnetic interactions can both generate and destroy entanglement depending on the initial state preparation.
main_problem: The study investigates how quantum entanglement evolves between two electrons trapped harmonically and interacting via electromagnetic forces.
main_result: The interaction can either generate entanglement if starting from a single-mode squeezed state or cause the degradation of pre-existing entanglement if starting from a two-mode squeezed state.
method: The analysis employs the covariance matrix formalism to track the time evolution of Gaussian states, quantifying entanglement using the logarithmic negativity.
model_or_system: The system consists of two electrons in adjacent harmonic traps, governed by a Hamiltonian including Coulomb and Darwin interaction terms. The dynamics are analyzed for multi-mode Gaussian states at thermal equilibrium.
key_observables: Logarithmic Negativity (EN), which quantifies the degree of entanglement.
important_parameters: Squeezing coefficient ($\xi$), temperature ($T$) or thermal occupation number ($N$), and interaction coupling constants ($g_C, g_D$).
main_assumptions: The system is treated as a multi-mode Gaussian state at thermal equilibrium, and the interaction Hamiltonian is approximated by expanding terms assuming trap separation $d$ is much larger than electron fluctuations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of EN for both single-mode and two-mode squeezed initial states under varying squeezing levels and noise/temperature conditions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical model and Hamiltonian, to detailing the mathematical methods (covariance matrix formalism), presenting analytical solutions for time evolution operators, and finally analyzing the results for different initial entanglement configurations.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses fundamental questions in open quantum systems and trapped-ion physics by quantifying how environmental coupling (thermal noise) and internal interactions affect fragile quantum correlations like entanglement.
